title: Senegalese Paella with Dried Saloum Seafood
localName: Paella sénégalaise — riz aux fruits de mer séchés du Saloum
author: Lamine Faye
desc: A thiebou yapp-style rice with the Saloum dried-shellfish set — guedj, yet, dried shrimp, tuffa, yokhos and pagne — and a faint measure of nététou.
longDesc: Lamine Faye’s ‘paella sénégalaise’ is a thiebou yapp (rice with meat) cooked with the dried seafood of the Saloum islands. A kilo of broken rice, 800 g of beef or lamb, two large onions, four garlic cloves, two tablespoons of tomato concentrate and three fresh tomatoes make the base, with a nokkos of onion, garlic, parsley, pepper, chile, a stock cube and a little nététou, and vegetables of choice. The dried set — a piece of guedj Yass, a piece of yet, tuffa, yokhos, a handful of dried shrimp and pagne — goes in to release its flavour. The five steps give no time or temperature.
ingredients: Nokkos: onion, garlic, parsley, pepper, chile, stock cube, plus a little nététou in small quantity — amounts not printed
Carrots, cabbage, cassava, aubergine, as chosen — quantities not printed
Oil, salt, pepper, chile — quantities not printed
steps: Fry the meat and the onions. Add the tomato concentrate and fresh tomatoes.
Pound the nokkos and add it with a little nététou.
Add water, then the dried seafood: guedj, yet, tuffa, yokhos, pagne and dried shrimp. Simmer so that all the flavours are released.
Cook the vegetables; once tender, take them out and set aside with the meat.
Add the rice to the broth and cook until done; serve the meat and vegetables on top.
chefTips: The source’s two cues are ‘once tender, remove and set aside with the meat’ and ‘let it simmer so that all the flavours are released’.
The five printed steps contain no time or temperature; the only figures are the header times (30 minutes preparation, 1 hour cooking).
Use nététou sparingly — the page says ‘en faible quantité’.
The dried-seafood names (tuffa, yokhos, pagne) are the page’s own and are not glossed.
commonMistakes: Over-salting before the dried seafood has been tasted.
reheating: Steam gently with a splash of water.
healthBenefits: Dried shrimp and fish add calcium and protein.
culturalNote: The page is also a shop for the author’s dried seafood, so the product is the point as well as the recipe; it is the only source found that names the Saloum dried-shellfish set together. The ‘paella’ label is the author’s own.
sources: Source: seggfaye.com, byline ‘Par Lamine Faye, le Guedjologue’, published 22 June 2026. SINGLE-PASS. Yield: ‘6 pers.’ Preparation 30 min, cooking 1 h, total 1 h 30.
COMMERCIAL FLAG: the page sells dried seafood. Recorded as a conflict of interest; the recipe figures are still the author’s own.

The five method steps contain no time, temperature or numeric quantity. The only figures are the header timings. Cues in short fragments: ‘Une fois tendres, retirez-les et réservez-les avec la viande’; ‘Laissez mijoter le temps que toutes les saveurs se libèrent’.
The page presents the dish as ‘façon thiebou yapp’. Regional attribution is to the Saloum islands; no ethnic group is named.
The water and rice-to-liquid ratio are not printed anywhere.
